# Master's Research — Liver Viability & ICG-NIR

My Master's research focuses on developing an ex vivo liver perfusion platform and using ICG-NIR
kinetics to investigate quantitative indicators of liver function and viability.

## Objective 1 — Ex Vivo Perfusion Platform

Build and validate a stable experimental platform capable of maintaining rat livers under controlled
physiological conditions.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["Reservoir"] --> B["Peristaltic Pump"]
    B --> C["Pulse Damper"]
    C --> D["Flow Sensor"]
    D --> E["Oxygenator"]
    E --> F["Bubble Trap"]
    F --> G["Liver"]
    G --> H["Return"]
```

## Objective 2 — Baseline Physiological Dataset

Characterize the physiological and experimental baseline before introducing ICG. The aim is to
determine the expected range and variability of pressure, flow, temperature, vascular resistance,
pH and gases under stable perfusion.

  <div class="slot-label">

## Objective 3 — ICG-NIR Functional Marker

Develop a quantitative functional marker from ICG fluorescence kinetics.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["ICG + albumin"] --> B["Liver uptake"]
    B --> C["NIR fluorescence"]
    C --> D["FI(t)"]
    D --> E["PDR / R15 / CLR / other parameters"]
    E --> F["Functional assessment"]
```

# Engineering Approach

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["Understand problem"] --> B["Identify measurable variables"]
    B --> C["Review literature / existing systems"]
    C --> D["Define requirements"]
    D --> E["Prototype"]
    E --> F["Measure"]
    F --> G["Compare"]
    G --> H["Redesign"]
    H --> I["Validate"]
    I --> J["Integrate & document"]
```
